claims.claim: Both EHT pol+ and EHT pol- cells express reporters driven by the hematopoietic marker CD41.
claims.source: We also observed that both EHT pol+and EHT pol- cells express reporters driven by the hematopoietic marker CD41 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), which indicates that they are both endowed with hematopoietic potential.
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data showing CD41 expression.

claims.claim: HE cells do not appear to be polarized at the initiation of the EHT time-window based on the absence of Podxl2 enrichment at luminal membranes.
claims.source: Surprisingly, confocal microscopy using our eGFP-podxl2 and mKate2-podxl2 expressing fish lines revealed that HE cells do not appear to be polarized, based on the absence of Podxl2 enrichment at luminal membranes, at the initiation of the EHT time-window and later (at approximately 28–30 hpf, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 see also at 35 hpf Figure 2A, top left panel, green arrows and Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and at 48–55 hpf Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data.

claims.claim: The cytoplasm of HE cells is filled with membrane vesicles that carry eGFP-podxl2.
claims.source: Interestingly, the cytoplasm of characteristic elongated HE cells located on the aortic floor is filled with more-or-less large membrane vesicles that carry eGFP-podxl2 (the largest vesicles reaching approximately 30 µm in diameter).
claims.evidence: This is based on confocal microscopy observations.

claims.claim: Loss of apicobasal polarity features of HE cells at 28-30 hpf may be part of the programme that initiates the EHT process.
claims.source: Consequently, loss of apicobasal polarity features of HE cells at 28–30 hpf may be part of the programme that initiates the EHT process.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of non-polarized HE cells.

claims.claim: Expression of dt-runx1 leads to accumulation of HE cells in comparison to controls.
claims.source: Firstly, using 48–55 hpf Tg(dt-runx1) embryos and live imaging we observed, in comparison to controls, a significant accumulation of HE cells (see Figure 3A, top and bottom panels (HE, arrowheads), see also the quantifications Figure 3B, top graph, median value of 17 cells for controls and 25 cells for mutants).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of live imaging data.

claims.claim: Expression of dt-runx1 leads to an increase in the proportion of EHT pol+ cells.
claims.source: We also observed the unusual tendency for the accumulation of EHT pol+ cells (Figure 3A, green and pink arrows), with a maximum value of 3 cells per embryo for controls that reached the unusual - never observed in control conditions -, values of 11, 9, and 8 cells for 3 mutants out of 7 (Figure 3B, middle graph).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of imaging data.

claims.claim: Expression of dt-runx1 does not significantly modify the number of EHT pol- cells.
claims.source: Finally, we did not observe any significant modification in the number of EHT pol- cells (same median values for both controls and mutants, the values oscillating between 0 and 1 cell per embryo, with only one example of an embryo exhibiting two apparent EHT pol- cells [Figure 3B, bottom graph]).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data.

claims.claim: Cells that accumulate in the aortic floor of dt-Runx1 mutants are of hematopoietic nature.
claims.source: Secondly, using 48–55 hpf Tg(dt-runx1) embryos and controls Tg(Kdrl:eGFP) we confirm, by whole mount in situ hybridization performed with an RNAscope probe specific for myb (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), that the cells that accumulate in the aortic floor of dt-Runx1 mutants are indeed of hematopoietic nature (see the cells with RNAscope spots in magenta or marked by blue arrows, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, zoomed areas).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data.

claims.claim: There is a specific increase of hemogenic/EHT cells in aortic floors of dt-Runx1 mutants in comparison to controls.
claims.source: However, cell counts after segmentation using the Imaris software confirmed, based on cell localization, the specific increase of hemogenic/EHT cells in aortic floors of mutants median values of 34 and 16.5 for mutants and controls, respectively, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B (right panel) while no difference was measured for endothelial roof cells between mutants and controls (left panel).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of RNAscope data.

claims.claim: The increase of pre-hematopoietic cells in the aortic floor in dt-Runx1 mutants correlates with a decrease in hematopoietic cells lodging in the sub-aortic region.
claims.source: Importantly, the increase of pre-hematopoietic cells in the aortic floor in the mutants correlates with a decrease in hematopoietic cells lodging in the sub-aortic region, reinforcing the idea of impairment in EHT cell emergence (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, right panel).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cell counts in different regions.

claims.claim: There is an important increase in myb expression by hemogenic cells in the floor of dt-Runx1 mutants in comparison to controls.
claims.source: Finally, quantification of the number of myb RNAscope spots per segmented hemogenic cells highlights the important increase in expression by hemogenic cells in the floor of dt-Runx1 mutants, in comparison to controls (with median values of 4 and 0, respectively) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, right panel).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of RNAscope data.

claims.claim: Embryos obtained from outcrossing Tg(dt-runx1) and Tg(Kdrl:mKate2-podxl2) fishes contain polarized HE cells based on enrichment of the polarity marker at luminal membranes.
claims.source: Thirdly, between 30 and 55 hpf, using live confocal microscopy and contrarily to what we observed with our fish lines expressing either eGFP-podxl2 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2) or mKate2-podxl2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) in which HE cells appear to be non-polarized, embryos obtained from outcrossing Tg(dt-runx1) and Tg(Kdrl:mKate2-podxl2) fishes appear to contain polarized HE cells, based on enrichment of the polarity marker at luminal membranes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is based on confocal microscopy observations.

claims.claim: Hematopoiesis is affected at 5 dpf in dt-Runx1 mutants as shown by a significant increase in the number of hematopoietic cells in the thymus.
claims.source: Fifthly, hematopoiesis is affected far downstream of emergence, as attested by the significant increase, at 5 dpf, in the number of hematopoietic cells in the thymus of dt-Runx1 mutants, in comparison to control siblings (see Figure 3—figure supplement 3A for images after cell segmentation with the Imaris software accompanied by Figure 3—video 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B for quantifications showing significant increase in thymus volume [left panel] owed to the increase in cell number [middle panel] rather than in cell volume [right panel]).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of thymus morphometry.

claims.claim: Pard3ba mRNAs are expressed in the aorta during the EHT time-window.
claims.source: Among the four Pard3 proteins expressed in the zebrafish (encoded by four different genes and non-including splicing variants), we describe the specific expression of Pard3ba, in the aorta, during the EHT time-window.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data.

claims.claim: The expression of Pard3ba is sensitive to interference with the transcription factor Runx1.
claims.source: We show that the expression of Pard3ba is sensitive to interference with the transcription factor Runx1 whose function is essential for EHT completion (Kissa and Herbomel, 2010) and for regulating HSC number (Adamo et al., 2009; North et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and RNAscope data comparing control and dt-Runx1 conditions.

claims.claim: Pard3ba mRNAs are localized heterogeneously along the aortic axis with enrichment in specific regions (MERs).
claims.source: To visualize more precisely expression levels in the vascular system in the trunk (more specifically in the aorta and the underlying vein), we zoomed in this region (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D) and observed a homogeneous localization of Pard3aa and Pard3ab mRNAs as well as, strikingly in the case of Pard3ba, a quite heterogeneous localization of mRNAs unequally concentrated along the aortic axis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D middle panel and see also Figure 4C, top panel; these will be referred thereon as Pard3ba mRNA enriched regions (MERs)).
claims.evidence: This is based on RNAscope in situ hybridization data.

claims.claim: Expression of dt-Runx1 leads to an increase of approximately 300% in Pard3ba spots per aortic segment.
claims.source: Quantification of RNAscope spots per aortic segment and per hemogenic/EHT cell using Imaris revealed an increase of almost 300% for the former when comparing controls and mutants (median values of 65.00 and 167.50 for controls and dt-Runx1 mutants, respectively, Figure 4D) and that virtually no Pard3ba mRNA was detected in the latter (median values of 0.00 spots per hemogenic/EHT cell for both controls and dt-Runx1 mutants, Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of RNAscope data.

claims.claim: Pard3ba mRNAs are preferentially localized in the direct vicinity of hemogenic/EHT cells.
claims.source: Finally and importantly, in wild-type embryos, the Pard3ba mRNAs are preferentially localized in the direct vicinity of hemogenic/EHT cells (Figure 4F and G).
claims.evidence: This is based on spatial analysis of RNAscope data.

claims.claim: More than 50% of Pard3ba spots are localized within 5-10 µm of hemogenic/EHT cells.
claims.source: Indeed, more than 50% of Pard3ba spots are localized within 5–10 µm of hemogenic/EHT cells (Figure 4G, middle panel), and more than 75% of spots are localized within a 5–20 µm distance (Figure 4G right panel).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative spatial analysis of RNAscope data.

claims.claim: The number of hemogenic/EHT cells strongly correlates with the spatial densification of Pard3ba spots around hemogenic/EHT cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, the number of hemogenic/EHT cells does not correlate with the absolute number of spots (Figure 4F, left panel, R=0.34), but rather it strongly correlates with the spatial densification of spots around hemogenic/EHT cells: the shorter the distance of the majority of spots are of hemogenic/EHT cells (Figure 4F, middle and right panel, representing 50% and 75% of spots, respectively), the higher the hemogenic/EHT cell count (R=–0.84 and R=–0.83, respectively).
claims.evidence: This is based on correlation analysis of spatial RNAscope data.

claims.claim: AECs expressing Pard3ba mRNAs are mostly in direct contact with cells committed to undergo EHT.
claims.source: This shows that AECs expressing Pard3ba mRNAs are mostly in direct contact with cells committed to undergo EHT and suggests a signalling crosstalk occurring between them.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the spatial proximity of Pard3ba expression to hemogenic/EHT cells.

claims.claim: Tri-junctional pools localized at antero-posterior poles of EHT cells enriched with eGFP-Jam3b molecules are significantly more dynamic for EHT pol+ cells in comparison to EHT pol- cells.
claims.source: Altogether and unexpectedly regarding our initial scenario, these results indicate that tri-junctional pools localized at antero-posterior poles of EHT cells and enriched with eGFP-Jam3b molecules are significantly more dynamic for EHT pol+ cells in comparison to EHT pol- cells.
claims.evidence: This is based on FRAP measurements comparing the two cell types.

claims.claim: The median value of early recovery slopes for EHT pol+ - EC versus EHT pol- - EC junctional interfaces is increased by 128%.
claims.source: Although smaller, differences in recovery were also measured between EHT pol+ – EC and EHT pol- – EC junctional interfaces when focusing on the earliest time points (the first 30 s, Figure 6F), with the median value of early recovery slopes for the EHT pol+ - EC versus EHT pol- – EC junctional interfaces increased by 128% (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of FRAP data.

claims.claim: ArhGEF11, ArhGEF12b, Tiam1b and Tiam2a are significantly reduced upon dt-runx1 expression at 48 hpf.
claims.source: We found that, in comparison to controls, ArhGEF11, ArhGEF12b, Tiam1b and Tiam2a are significantly reduced upon dt-runx1 expression at 48 hpf, hence being positively controlled in the wild-type condition, when the emergence of EHT cells is peaking.
claims.evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data comparing control and dt-runx1 conditions.

claims.claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to accumulation of hemogenic cells in the aortic floor.
claims.source: For the morphants, we found approximately a double amount of hemogenic cells in the aortic floor in comparison to controls (altogether localized on the floor and on the lateral sides of the aorta, see Figure 7A, panels in (a) for 2D-cartographies to visualize cell shapes, with the accumulation of hemogenic cells delineated in yellow for one morphant on the right and panels in (a') for cell counts of endothelial, hemogenic and EHT cells either in the entire aorta in trunks [left] or, more precisely, the aortic floor and lateral aortic side and the roof[right]; see also Figure 7—figure supplement 5 for additional examples).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative morphometric analysis of confocal imaging data.

claims.claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to a significant reduction in the number of morphologically characterized EHT cells.
claims.source: This is accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of morphologically characterized EHT cells (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 5).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cell counts from imaging data.

claims.claim: A significant increase in the aortic perimeter was found for ArhGEF11 morphants.
claims.source: Consistently, a significant increase in the aortic perimeter was found, at least for the morphants (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is based on morphometric measurements from imaging data.

claims.claim: Hemogenic cells in ArhGEF11 morphants are on average less elongated in comparison to control and to the CRISPR homozygous mutants.
claims.source: Of notice also, hemogenic cells in morphants are on average less elongated in comparison to control and to the CRISPR homozygous mutants (as well as less dispersed according to this parameter, compare Figure 7A, panel (a''') with Figure 7B, panel (b'''), with visualization of the dispersion on right panels).
claims.evidence: This is based on morphometric analysis of cell shape from imaging data.

claims.claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to an increase in the number of hemogenic/EHT cells in the aortic floor.
claims.source: We show that, in agreement with our morphometric analysis, an increase in the number of hemogenic/EHT cells in the aortic floor in morphants in comparison to control embryos (Figure 7—figure supplement 7D, with median values of 14.0 and 22.5 hemogenic/EHT cells for controls and morphants, respectively).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of CD41:eGFP expressing cells.

claims.claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to a relative diminution in the number of newly generated HSPC precursors.
claims.source: Additionally, we observe, despite the high variability in both controls and morphants, a relative diminution in the number of newly generated HSPC precursors (Figure 7—figure supplement 7E, with median values of 22.0 and 16.5 HSPCs for controls and morphants, respectively).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of CD41:eGFP expressing cells that are kdrl-negative.

claims.claim: ArhGEF11 exerts important functions in the EHT process.
claims.source: Altogether, the morphants and CRISPR mutant phenotypes show that the progression throughout EHT is significantly impaired supporting the idea that ArhGEF11 exerts important functions in the process.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypes observed upon ArhGEF11 interference.

claims.claim: In ArhGEF11 morphants, there is an increase in FRAP recovery parameters for eGFP-Jam3b pools at the tri-junctional HE-HE-EC interface in comparison to controls.
claims.source: In the case of the MO treatment (in which case HE cells accumulate on the aortic floor, see the 2D cartography (Figure 8A)) we measured, in comparison to controls, an increase in FRAP recovery parameters for eGFP-Jam3b pools at the tri-junctional HE-HE-EC interface, with a prominent tendency for an increase in the recovery speed at early time points (Figure 8B, panel (b'''), values obtained from fluorescence intensity recoveries whose mean values are represented by curves in panel (b''); compare with maximum recovery amplitudes (b'), with values obtained from the plateaus of fluorescence recovery intensities whose mean values are represented in panel (b)).
claims.evidence: This is based on FRAP measurements at specific junctional interfaces.

claims.claim: In ArhGEF11 CRISPR C-terminal deletion mutants, there is a small tendency for an increase in the mobile pool at HE-EC-EC tri-junctions.
claims.source: Results are different for the ArhGEF11CRISPR-Cterdel+/+ homozygous mutants for which we did not observe any obvious effect at HE-HE-EC tri-junctions (Figure 8C, with the panels (c - c''') mirroring the presentations of results obtained for morphants and internal controls in Figure 8B) but, rather, a small tendency for an increase in the mobile pool at HE-EC-EC tri-junctions (that has the particularity to concern 2 endothelial cells that contact the longitudinal membrane of one HE cell, see Figure 8A and D).
claims.evidence: This is based on FRAP measurements at specific junctional interfaces.

results.result: Two distinct cell types emerge from the aortic floor with radically different morphodynamics: EHT pol+ cells characterized by reinforcement of apicobasal polarity and maintenance of the apical/luminal membrane, and EHT pol- cells emerging via a process reminiscent of trans-endothelial migration without enrichment of polarity markers at the luminal membrane. Both cell types express hematopoietic markers and maintain their morphological characteristics after division, with an approximate ratio of 2:1 (EHT pol+:EHT pol-).
results.evaluation: Claims C2-C4, C17-C22 provide converging evidence from live imaging with polarity markers (eGFP-podxl2, mKate2-podxl2) showing two morphologically and molecularly distinct EHT cell types. The data include time-lapse imaging, quantitative cell counts, and CD41 expression analysis. The ratio estimation and division observations are based on systematic imaging across multiple embryos and time windows.

results.result: HE cells do not appear to be polarized at the initiation of the EHT time-window (28-30 hpf) based on the absence of Podxl2 enrichment at luminal membranes. Instead, HE cell cytoplasm is filled with membrane vesicles carrying eGFP-podxl2, suggesting that loss of apicobasal polarity may be part of the programme initiating the EHT process.
results.evaluation: Claims C23-C25 are supported by confocal microscopy data showing equal partitioning of Podxl2 between luminal and basal membranes in HE cells, contrasting with polarized aortic endothelial cells. The presence of large intracellular vesicles (up to 30 µm) is documented. The inference about EHT initiation (C25) is reasonable given the temporal correlation and comparison with later polarized EHT pol+ cells.

results.result: Interfering with Runx1 function using a dominant-negative mutant (dt-runx1) leads to accumulation of HE cells, increased proportion of EHT pol+ cells (particularly in lateral positions), maintenance of HE cell polarity, increased myb expression in hemogenic cells, decreased sub-aortic hematopoietic cells, and increased thymus cellularity at 5 dpf. The balance between EHT pol+ and pol- emergence types depends on tuning apicobasal polarity at the HE level.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C26-C34 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: live imaging with quantitative cell counts (C26-C28), RNAscope in situ hybridization with spatial analysis (C29-C32), confocal microscopy of polarity markers (C33), and thymus morphometry (C34). The dt-runx1 mutant produces a consistent phenotype across multiple readouts. However, the mechanism by which Runx1 controls polarity (C5) remains inferential, though well-supported by the accumulation of polarized HE cells and EHT pol+ cells.

results.result: Pard3ba, one of four Pard3 proteins in zebrafish, is expressed in the aorta during the EHT time-window with heterogeneous spatial distribution along the aortic axis (mRNA enriched regions, MERs). Pard3ba expression is sensitive to Runx1 interference, showing ~300% increase in dt-Runx1 mutants. Pard3ba mRNAs are preferentially localized in aortic endothelial cells (AECs) in direct vicinity of hemogenic/EHT cells (>50% within 5-10 µm), and the spatial densification of Pard3ba spots strongly correlates with hemogenic/EHT cell count (R=-0.84), suggesting signaling crosstalk between aortic and hemogenic cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C35-C42 are supported by qRT-PCR on FACS-sorted cells and RNAscope in situ hybridization with quantitative spatial analysis. The specificity of Pard3ba response to Runx1 interference is demonstrated by comparison with other Pard3 family members. The spatial correlation analysis (C41) is rigorous with strong correlation coefficients. The inference of signaling crosstalk (C42) is reasonable given the spatial proximity data, though the molecular mechanism remains to be determined.

results.result: Tri-junctional pools enriched with eGFP-Jam3b molecules at antero-posterior poles of EHT cells are significantly more dynamic for EHT pol+ cells compared to EHT pol- cells, with 128% increase in median early recovery slopes at EHT pol+ - EC versus EHT pol- - EC junctional interfaces.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C44 are supported by FRAP measurements on transgenic embryos expressing eGFP-Jam3b. The analysis includes appropriate controls (EC-EC junctions) and quantitative metrics (recovery slopes, maximum amplitude). The result is counterintuitive to the authors' initial hypothesis but is supported by the data. Sample sizes appear adequate (n values stated in figures), though the high biological variability noted by the authors suggests caution in interpretation.

results.result: ArhGEF11, ArhGEF12b, Tiam1b, and Tiam2a expression levels are significantly reduced upon dt-runx1 expression at 48 hpf, indicating positive regulation by Runx1 during peak EHT emergence.
results.evaluation: Claim C45 is supported by qRT-PCR data comparing control and dt-runx1 conditions with statistical significance. The analysis was performed on trunk dissections at the appropriate developmental stage. This result provides a molecular link between Runx1 activity and cytoskeletal regulation during EHT.

results.result: ArhGEF11/PDZ-RhoGEF plays an essential role in controlling the HE-endothelial cell dynamic interface and cell-cell intercalation required for EHT completion. Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing (morpholino) or C-terminal deletion (CRISPR) leads to accumulation of hemogenic cells in the aortic floor, reduction in morphologically characterized EHT cells, increased aortic perimeter, altered hemogenic cell morphology, and decreased HSPC generation.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C9, C46-C52 are supported by complementary genetic approaches (morpholino and CRISPR) with consistent phenotypes. The analysis includes quantitative morphometry of cell shape, position, and counts using semi-automated segmentation. The CD41:eGFP analysis (C50-C51) provides functional validation of impaired hematopoiesis. The phenotypic differences between morpholino and CRISPR mutants (C49) are noted and discussed appropriately. The inference about intercalation (C9) is supported by the accumulation of cells and morphological changes.

results.result: ArhGEF11 interference differentially affects junctional dynamics at distinct tri-cellular interfaces: morpholino treatment increases FRAP recovery parameters at HE-HE-EC tri-junctions (particularly early recovery speed), while CRISPR C-terminal deletion mutants show a tendency for increased mobile pool at HE-EC-EC tri-junctions.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C54 are supported by FRAP measurements at specific junctional interfaces identified using 2D cartography. The differential effects of morpholino versus CRISPR mutants suggest distinct functions of the exon 38-encoded region versus the C-terminus. However, the CRISPR result (C54) is described as a 'small tendency,' indicating weaker statistical support. The biological interpretation is complex and the authors appropriately note the limitations.

results.result: Background knowledge claims establishing that hematopoietic stem cells emerge from the hemogenic endothelium in the AGM region during a narrow developmental time window, with the HE characterized by inherent heterogeneity contributing to both pre-HSCs and more restricted progenitors.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C10-C16 represent established knowledge in the field, supported by appropriate citations to seminal studies. These provide necessary context for the current work and are accurately represented.

results.result: There is a signaling crosstalk controlling cell polarity and its associated features between aortic and hemogenic cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C7 is inferred from the observation that Pard3ba expression in aortic cells is sensitive to Runx1 activity (C6) and the spatial proximity of Pard3ba-expressing cells to hemogenic/EHT cells (C39-C42). While the spatial and molecular data are supportive, the claim of 'signaling crosstalk' implies bidirectional communication and specific molecular mechanisms that have not been directly demonstrated. The authors appropriately present this as a hypothesis in the discussion, noting alternative explanations (e.g., shared developmental history of aortic and HE cells).

results.result: The authors identify two distinct cell types emerging from the aortic floor during EHT with radically different morphodynamics: EHT pol+ cells characterized by enrichment of podocalyxin at the luminal membrane and maintenance of apicobasal polarity, and EHT pol- cells lacking this enrichment, emerging via a process reminiscent of trans-endothelial migration. Both cell types express hematopoietic markers and divide during emergence while maintaining their morphological characteristics, with an approximate 2:1 ratio of pol+ to pol- cells.
results.evaluation: Both reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. The first reviewer states 'The evidence supporting the existence of these two distinct morphologies is convincing, using state-of-the-art confocal microscopy and image analysis of 2D-cartography.' The second reviewer confirms 'They demonstrate that differences in apico-basal polarity are strongly associated with different cellular morphologies of cells undergoing EHT from HE (EHT pol- and EHT pol+)' and notes 'The evidence for the different cellular morphologies of cells undergoing EHT is strong.'

results.result: Interfering with Runx1 function using dt-runx1 expression leads to accumulation of hemogenic/EHT cells in the aortic floor, with a specific increase in EHT pol+ cells but not EHT pol- cells, and results in polarized HE cells (contrary to wild-type where HE cells appear non-polarized). This suggests that the balance between the two emergence types depends on tuning apicobasal polarity at the level of the HE.
results.evaluation: The reviewers accept these findings without challenge. The second reviewer notes 'They then overexpress a truncated form of Runx1 (just the runt domain) to block Runx1 function and show that more HE cells abort EHT and remain associated with the embryonic dorsal aorta.' The imaging data quality is praised as 'excellent' and the approach is described as 'elegant,' indicating acceptance of the experimental results and their interpretation regarding polarity regulation.

results.result: Pard3ba, one of four Pard3 proteins in zebrafish, is expressed in the aorta during the EHT time-window with heterogeneous localization along the aortic axis. Its expression is sensitive to Runx1 interference, showing a ~300% increase in dt-Runx1 mutants. Pard3ba mRNAs are preferentially localized in the direct vicinity of hemogenic/EHT cells, suggesting signaling crosstalk between aortic and hemogenic cells controlling cell polarity.
results.evaluation: The second reviewer acknowledges this finding, stating 'The revised version identifies pard3ab as differentially distributed in dtRunx mutants and correlates that distribution with a potential regulatory role on cell polarity.' While the reviewer notes 'No direct evidence for their role in EHT is presented,' they do not challenge the observational data or the correlation findings, accepting the descriptive results while noting the limitation regarding mechanistic proof.

results.result: There is a signaling crosstalk controlling cell polarity and its associated features between aortic and hemogenic cells, inferred from the observation that Pard3ba expression in aortic cells is sensitive to Runx1 activity.
results.evaluation: The second reviewer explicitly notes 'No direct evidence for their role in EHT is presented,' indicating that while the correlation between Pard3ba distribution and Runx1 activity is accepted, the mechanistic claim of signaling crosstalk remains unproven. The reviewer accepts the correlation but questions whether this constitutes evidence of functional crosstalk, leaving this interpretive claim in uncertain territory.

results.result: ArhGEF11/PDZ-RhoGEF plays an essential role in controlling the HE-endothelial cell dynamic interface, including cell-cell intercalation required for emergence completion. Interfering with ArhGEF11 through morpholino or CRISPR leads to accumulation of hemogenic cells in the aortic floor, reduction in morphologically characterized EHT cells, and impaired EHT progression. ArhGEF11 expression is positively controlled by Runx1.
results.evaluation: The reviewers do not raise concerns about these findings. The second reviewer states 'the main claim that tuning apico-basal polarity and junctional recycling underlie morphological complexity of EHT (rather than of HSCs) is well supported by the data,' which encompasses the ArhGEF11 functional data. The imaging data quality is described as 'excellent,' and the experimental approaches are accepted without challenge.

results.result: Tri-junctional pools enriched with Jam3b molecules show differential dynamics between EHT pol+ and pol- cells, with pol+ cells exhibiting significantly more dynamic junctions. Interfering with ArhGEF11 alters FRAP recovery parameters at specific junctional interfaces, with morpholino treatment increasing recovery at HE-HE-EC interfaces and CRISPR mutants showing effects at HE-EC-EC tri-junctions.
results.evaluation: The reviewers accept these findings as part of the overall evidence for junctional dynamics. The second reviewer explicitly states 'the main claim that tuning apico-basal polarity and junctional recycling underlie morphological complexity of EHT (rather than of HSCs) is well supported by the data,' directly affirming the junctional recycling/dynamics data. No concerns are raised about the FRAP methodology or interpretation.

results.result: HE cells do not appear to be polarized at the initiation of the EHT time-window based on the absence of Podxl2 enrichment at luminal membranes. The cytoplasm of HE cells is filled with membrane vesicles carrying podxl2. Loss of apicobasal polarity features may be part of the programme that initiates the EHT process.
results.evaluation: The reviewers do not challenge these observations. The first reviewer notes the study 'brings new information on how regulation of apico-basal polarity influences cellular behaviour,' implicitly accepting the observations about HE cell polarity status. The second reviewer confirms the evidence is 'strong' for the polarity-related findings and does not raise concerns about the HE cell characterization.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2-C4, C17-C22 regarding two morphologically distinct EHT cell types. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with strong endorsement of the imaging evidence and quantitative analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the confocal microscopy and 2D-cartography approaches.

Perfect agreement on claims C23-C25 regarding Podxl2 partitioning in HE cells and EHT initiation. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these observations as part of the polarity-related findings without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C5, C26-C34 regarding Runx1's role in polarity regulation. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe the dt-runx1 approach as 'elegant' and accept the accumulation of polarized HE cells as evidence, though both note the mechanism remains somewhat inferential.

Agreement on claims C6, C35-C42 regarding Pard3ba expression and spatial correlation. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. However, peer reviewers note 'No direct evidence for their role in EHT is presented,' accepting the descriptive/correlational data while acknowledging mechanistic limitations.

Agreement on claim C7 regarding signaling crosstalk. Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the claim implies bidirectional communication not directly demonstrated; peer reviewers similarly state 'No direct evidence for their role in EHT is presented,' accepting correlation but questioning mechanistic proof.

Strong agreement on claims C8-C9, C46-C52 regarding ArhGEF11 function and intercalation. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the genetic approaches and morphometric analysis without challenge, noting 'excellent' imaging data quality. OpenEval R7 includes C45 which peer R5 does not explicitly address.

Agreement on claims C43-C44 regarding FRAP measurements of Jam3b dynamics. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm junctional recycling data as supporting the main claims. OpenEval notes high biological variability requiring cautious interpretation.

Agreement on claims C53-C54 regarding differential effects of morpholino versus CRISPR on junctional dynamics. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED.
